patterns.content: Prefer interface over type alias for object shapes that may be extended. Use type for unions/intersections: type Result<T> = Success<T> | Failure.
Discriminated unions: type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'rect'; w: number; h: number }. Switch on kind for exhaustive handling.
Use unknown instead of any for external data. Narrow with typeof, instanceof, or type guards before use. any disables type checking entirely.
Optional chaining and nullish coalescing: user?.address?.city ?? 'Unknown'. Avoids null checks cascade.
Generics with constraints: function getFirst<T extends { length: number }>(arr: T): T[0]. Use keyof for property key types.
async/await over raw Promises. try/catch for error handling. Promise.all for parallel awaits. Avoid .then() chains.
Mapped types for transformations: type Readonly<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }. Partial<T>, Required<T>, Pick<T, K> are built-in.
Utility types: ReturnType<typeof fn>, Parameters<typeof fn>, Awaited<Promise<T>>. Avoid reimplementing what the stdlib provides.
Const assertions: const config = { port: 3000, host: 'localhost' } as const — narrows types to literals, prevents mutation.
Zod or similar for runtime validation of external data. TypeScript types are compile-time only — validate at system boundaries (HTTP input, env vars).
